senses.gloss:
ITA-1.8.3.5 padārthaḥ पदार्थः
Object denoted by a word
Etymologically “the meaning or referent of a word”, it is applied to any entity that is knowable and nameable, i.e. an object of experience.

ITA-5.62.30 padminīkaṇṭakaḥ पद्मिनीकण्टकः
Papules resembling lotus thorns
A disorder characterized by patches with thorny projections; raised circular lesions; associated with itching; thorny projections resembling lotus thorns; painless; whitish projection.

ITA-3.13.31 Pādakurcāsthi पादकू र्चास्थि
Tarsal bones excluding talus and calcaneus

ITA-1.11.13 pādacatuṣṭayam पादचतुष्टयम्
Components of medical practice
These four components or elements are: the physician (vaidya, bhishak), materials for treatment (dravya), attendants or paramedics (upasthata) and the patient (rogi).

ITA-5.62.22 pādadārī पाददारी
Rhagades
A disorder characterized by fissuring and cracking of the feet; associated with pain.

ITA-5.2.1.45 pādadāhaḥ पाददाहः
Burning feet
A disorder characterized by burning sensation in feet.

ITA-3.9.17 pādamadhyam पादमध्यम्
Middle third of the foot, midfoot
Medial third of foot

ITA-5.2.1.46 pādaharṣaḥ पादहर्षः
Peripheral neuritis of the feet
A disorder characterized by numbness in feet; sensation of excitement/tingling in feet.

ITA-10.2.5 A quarter-portion protocol in which an unwholesome substance pādāṃśikakramaḥ is gradually withdrawn from the diet—one quarter on the first day, two quarters on the second day, three quarters on the third day—and replaced with the same amount of a non-addictive wholesome alternative. One quarter unwholesome plus three quarters non-addictive wholesome substance should be maintained on the fourth, fifth and sixth days. On the seventh day the unwholesome substance should be completely discarded and the wholesome substance continued thereafter. This method is generally employed for de-addiction purposes. पादांशिकक्रमः
Diet-transition protocol

ITA-3.9.14 pādāgram पादाग्रम्
Forefoot
The anterior third of the foot.

ITA-9.2.33 pādāghātaḥ पादाघातः
Therapeutic pedal massage
A therapeutic massage in which the feet are used to apply body weight as pressure.
